source: Class defaults for a water-cooled spark-ignition passenger-car engine (engine thermal plan T1, out/engine_thermal_plan.md, vault PHYS-063). A part file meant to be extended: it carries no displacement_l, so it is not loadable on its own - an engine-specific file extends it and adds displacement_l. Capacities [D]: engine lump 26600 J/K per litre = 25 kg/L participating metal [AS] x 630 J/(kg K) (0.62 x cast iron 460 + 0.38 x aluminium 900, 62 % cast-iron share [C Haury & Volkering, Chalmers MSc 2011:13, S5]) + 3.0 L/L coolant [AS] x 1065 kg/m3 x 3400 J/(kg K) [AS, 50/50 ethylene glycol]; oil lump 7600 J/K per litre = 2.25 L/L oil [AS] x 851 kg/m3 [C S8] x 2000 J/(kg K) [AS] + 6 kg/L crank and sump metal [AS] x 630. wall_heat_fraction 0.20 [AS], inside Heywood 1988 Table 12.1's 17-26 % coolant share of fuel energy for SI engines [C, secondhand, not re-verified] and equal to the exhaust-thermal branch's in_cylinder_wall_heat_fraction. friction_to_oil_fraction 0.30 [AS, calibration set]. motoring_friction_fraction 0.6 [D]: friction share of a graph engine's motoring curve (Heywood FMEP about 1.3 bar against about 0.9 bar pumping at 2000 rpm: 1.3/2.2 = 0.59); ignored by simulated engines. Oil: Mobil 1 ESP 5W-30 KV40 69.1 / KV100 12.0 mm2/s, density 0.851 g/ml at 15.6 C [C ExxonMobil product data sheet, read 2026-10-05, S8]; reference_temperature_c 95 [C vault PHYS-052: the friction maps come from EPA Ecotec motored friction at oil 92-98 C]; hydrodynamic_fraction 0.5 [D: solves k(20 C) in [2.0, 2.5], the cited 'about 2x to 2.5x' of Sandoval & Heywood SAE 2003-01-0725 / Roberts et al. 2014, with sqrt viscosity ratio 3.676 at 20 C]; friction_scale_min 1 and NO upper cap (owner 2026-10-05). T1b: k scales only the hydrodynamic part - the increment (k - 1) * F(n_ref) * sqrt(n / n_ref) is added to the map's speed-dependent part, the Coulomb/breakaway (boundary) friction is never scaled [C: Sandoval & Heywood scale only the hydrodynamic terms; fixed-load hydrodynamic friction ~ sqrt(mu * speed)]; hydrodynamic_reference_rpm 2000 [AS: mid-range of the friction maps, where the whole map is scaled by exactly k]. Validation against the cited cranking resistance of a 2 L SI engine vs oil viscosity (Europa Tabellenbuch Kfz via fahrzeug-elektrik.de/Eebd.htm, read 2026-10-05: 85 N*m at 2000 mm2/s, x1.45 at 5500 mm2/s, about 33 % at 100 mm2/s): the A25A at 120 rpm gives ratios 1.42 and 0.51 [M, out/thermal_t1b_progress.md]. Conductances per litre [AS]: oil-coolant time constant 300 s (G_oc = C_oil/tau_oc = 25.3 W/K per litre), block-air 7.5 W/K + 0.75 W/(K m/s) x ram speed (cool-down check C_e/G0 = 3547 s, about 1 h engine-off time constant), oil-air 2.5 + 0.25 per m/s. Pump 10 L/min per 1000 rpm per litre [AS]. Thermostat 88 -> 100 C opening range, 2 K play hysteresis, 20 s wax time constant [AS] (patent examples such as 88/100 C, attribution not verified). Water jacket (block cooling, 2026-10-16; every shipped engine extends this file and so carries it) [AS], sized for a passenger-car SI engine of 1.5-3 L: wetted area 0.2 m2 per litre (a 2 L I4: cylinder liners about 0.13 m2 for four 86 mm x 86 mm bores over the wetted liner height, plus the block's outer jacket wall and the head's coolant passages around ports and combustion-chamber roofs, about 0.4 m2 in all); coolant volume 3.0 L per litre = the 3.0 L/L this file's engine capacity already counts, so the metal lump is 25 kg/L x 630 J/(kg K) = 15750 J/K per litre and the total engine capacity is unchanged; htc_ref 5000 W/(m2 K) at 30 l/min per litre (the class pump at 3000 rpm), inside the 1000-20000 W/(m2 K) that forced convection of water/glycol reaches in engine coolant passages at 0.5-2 m/s (local nucleate boiling at the head's hot spots, which raises it further, is not modelled); flow_exponent 0.8 (Dittus-Boelter, Nu ~ Re^0.8 at fixed geometry [C Incropera & DeWitt eq. 8.60]); htc_min 500 W/(m2 K) for natural convection with the pump stopped. Effect [M, solve_steady_thermal with cooling_systems/sedan.json, 25 C, 2.0 L]: G_jacket = 2000 W/K at 3000 rpm, so a cruise load runs the metal a few K above the coolant and full load at high rpm about 10 K above it: 2.0 L at 3000 rpm, 12 kW wall heat, 25 m/s: metal 93.7 C over coolant 88.5 C (+5.1 K); A25A at 2000 rpm, 8 kW: +2.3 K; A25A at 6000 rpm, 45 kW wall heat, 40 m/s: metal 99.1 C over coolant 88.9 C (+10.1 K, G_jacket 4330 W/K).
